title: Certainty of cognition vs certainty of adhesion
source_text: XIII. Atque hic observandum venit fieri posse ut assensus moralis quodam respectu sit in animo firmior, eique tenacius & fortius adhaereat, quam assensus alius, qui nititur demonstratione, vel experientia. Quod ut intelligatur notanda est alia certitudinis distinctio quam Scholastici nonnulli proferunt. Nimirum alia est certitudo quae dici potest cognitionis, sive speculationis, alia vero quae certitudo adhaesionis vocatur. Prior illa certitudo pendet a sola convictione mentis, sed posterior etiam ab effectu voluntatis. Priorem objectum debite propositum a mente extorquet, non expectato voluntatis consensu. Posterior vero sequitur voluntatis imperium, & consensum. Quo major est illa certitudo, quae dicitur cognitionis, eo longius omnem dubitationem a mente removet. At quo major est ista, quam dicimus adhaesionis, eo mens assensum arctius amplectitur: & firmius retinet.
pass_a_gloss: And here it is to be observed that it can happen that moral assent is in a certain respect firmer in the soul, and adheres to it more tenaciously and strongly, than another assent which rests on demonstration or experience. Which that it may be understood, another distinction of certainty is to be noted which some Scholastics bring forward. Namely one certainty can be called of cognition, or of speculation; but another is called certainty of adhesion. That former certainty depends on the conviction of the mind alone, but the latter also on the effect of the will. The former a duly proposed object extorts from the mind, the consent of the will not being awaited. But the latter follows the empire and consent of the will. The greater that certainty which is called of cognition, the farther it removes every doubt from the mind. But the greater this which we call of adhesion, the more closely the mind embraces the assent and more firmly retains it.
pass_b_english: Moral assent can cling harder than demonstrative/experiential assent.
Cognition: mind-conviction alone, object-extorted. Adhesion: also will’s effect — closer cling.
